conventions.convention: The finite family has m ≥ 1; the true-null set is fixed under the specified law. FDP = V/max(R,1), FDR is its expectation, and FWER = P(V ≥ 1).
BH takes q ∈ (0,1), orders ties by original index, selects the largest qualifying rank using inclusive thresholds kq/m, and rejects no hypotheses when no rank qualifies.
The leave-one-out count uses thresholds (k+1)q/m on the remaining m−1 coordinates, includes zero in its maximum, and equals zero when m = 1.

The exact FDR equality assumes mutual independence of all p-values under every parameter law and exact uniformity of each true-null p-value. False-null laws are otherwise arbitrary. Null hypotheses are prespecified and nonempty.

load_bearing.statement: For m ≥ 1 p-values in [0,1] and q ∈ (0,1), order by (p_i,i), set R to the maximum of zero and all ranks k satisfying p_(k) ≤ kq/m, and reject exactly ranks 1 through R.
For measurable [0,1]-valued P_1,…,P_m, m ≥ 1 and q ∈ (0,1), S_i is measurable with respect to the other coordinates and, pointwise, I_i/max(R,1) = 1{P_i ≤ (S_i+1)q/m}/(S_i+1).
For a measurable rejection rule and fixed true-null set I_0, R counts all rejections and V counts rejected true nulls; FDP = V/max(R,1), FDR = E[FDP], and FWER = P(V ≥ 1).

For a prespecified finite family of nonempty null hypotheses with valid p-value statistics, if all m p-values are mutually independent under every P_θ and each true-null p-value satisfies P_θ(p_i ≤ u) = u for every u ∈ [0,1], then BH at every q ∈ (0,1) satisfies FDR_θ = (m_0(θ)/m)q ≤ q. False-null p-value laws may otherwise be arbitrary.

seams_checked.note: The two pages use compatible fixed-family, true-null, FDP denominator, FDR, and FWER conventions. The BH theorem explicitly strengthens marginal validity to exact uniformity and adds mutual independence; it does not import Bonferroni's arbitrary-dependence guarantee. Its nonempty-null restriction is explicit and compatible with the neighboring definition's allowance for vacuous empty nulls.

The downstream BH theorem and contribution lemma use the same largest-passing-rank procedure and cutoffs kq/m. The dependence page supplies separate PRDS and BY arguments and claims inequalities under their own hypotheses; it does not extend the independent theorem's exact equality to dependent or merely superuniform p-values. The BY procedure preserves the tie convention and uses its stated harmonic correction.
